editorial.headline: The Household-Goods Trade That Is Open Nationally, Closed to PMA in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This wholesale activity spans practical household goods and specialist supplies, but Bali’s permanent PMA moratorium changes the answer for foreign investors.
editorial.body:
This activity is a broad wholesale home for household goods and equipment that do not sit more neatly elsewhere. Its scope runs from cleaning tools and non-electric toothbrushes to electric bicycles, monowheels, hoverboards and scooters; recorded media on cassette, CD and DVD; and a substantial range of baby equipment, including prams, strollers, walkers, carriers and car seats. It also includes sports medals and trophies, tents and sleeping bags, promotional goods, imitation jewellery, household chemicals such as detergents and floor cleaners, and educational teaching aids.

That breadth is its defining feature. The activity is not organised around one product category or one retail setting, but around the wholesale distribution of varied household-related goods. A business using it may therefore deal in everyday domestic necessities alongside recreational, promotional, educational and specialist-use items, provided they fall within the stated scope. The record opens the activity to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar scales, so its commercial reach is not confined to one size of enterprise.

At the national level, the PMA position is TERBUKA, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. In plain terms, the national record permits this activity to have 100% foreign ownership. That is an important baseline, but it is not the complete answer for a business intending to register in Bali. National openness does not override the Bali-specific position recorded for this activity.

In Bali, a foreign investor cannot register this activity for PMA today. At the Besar scale, every scope is assessed in OSS as Rendah or Menengah-Rendah risk, bringing it within Bali’s island-wide, permanent moratorium on PMA for all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI. The Bali status is Blocked (risk class): the constraint is not a reduced foreign-share allowance, but a registration block under that moratorium, recorded as taking effect in May 2026. For a founder, the practical conclusion is crisp: the activity is nationally open to 100% foreign ownership, yet blocked for PMA registration in Bali under the stated risk-based rule.
editorial.pullQuote: National openness to 100% foreign ownership does not override Bali’s risk-based PMA registration block.
